data.summary: Fresh MAX investigation with explicitly labeled operator-prepared healthy save; no previous model context or future fix.
Unverified report: a unit reportedly disappears while entering a payload conveyor.
Fetching the exact revision and preparing build dependencies.
Build prepared. Investigation uses an isolated desktop with game network access disabled.
Restored the registered input files before this fresh game launch.
Testing the player report in the historical game build.

action.semantic: Open Play menu to access Load Game and import the supplied prepared save.
Open Load Game dialog.
Choose Import Save to load the operator-prepared fixture as saved gameplay state.
Wait for save-file chooser after activating Import Save.
Focus the save chooser filename field.
Enter the supplied operator fixture path.
Import the selected supplied save file.
Load the imported operator-prepared sandbox save into gameplay.

data.statement: The supplied gameplay save contains an identifiable Dagger and a connected payload-conveyor route; a Dagger entering it should be temporarily represented as a payload and emerge beyond the output rather than be lost.
data.prediction: After selecting and directing one Dagger to the route intake, its walking sprite will vanish at intake, then it will appear as a unit to the right of the third conveyor.
data.observation: Imported save card reports Sandbox / Wave 1 and has been loaded; route and units have not yet been identified on screen.

data.summary: Search pre-fix source for 'collapse UI hide hud Binding'.
Search pre-fix source for 'zoom in Binding.java'.

action.semantic: Toggle menus off to inspect units and the transport route without the build panel obscuring the view.
Zoom out around the units to locate the connected conveyor route and verify initial scene geometry.
Further zoom out centered on the conveyor intake so the full connected route and clear output can be inspected.
Enter RTS command mode and select the middle Dagger, keeping the other two units as visual controls.
Restore HUD to inspect RTS command controls and selection state.
Open pause menu to inspect command-mode control settings without altering the scene.
Open settings to inspect the RTS command-mode behavior.
Open control settings to locate command mode configuration.
Return to settings categories.
Open game settings to locate command-mode hold/toggle setting.
Toggle the Hold For Command Mode option to expose its current state and enable a persistent command-mode test workflow if needed.
Set command mode back to toggle behavior so its UI can remain visible after activating it.
Toggle Hold For Command Mode off using its row to retain a persistent RTS mode for inspection.
Move pointer away from the setting to distinguish hover highlighting from its actual toggle state.
Exit game settings after enabling toggle-style RTS command mode.
Return to paused gameplay.
Resume the loaded sandbox scene for the RTS transport test.
Activate persistent RTS command mode using the configured Shift binding.
Capture the pre-entry state: one outlined middle Dagger is selected in Command Mode and the right-facing payload conveyor route is visibly empty.
Choose the selected Dagger's Enter Payload Block command in Command Mode.
Assign the selected Dagger's Enter Payload Block target to the leftmost intake of the connected right-facing conveyor route.
Observe the selected Dagger as it reaches the commanded payload-conveyor intake.
Observe the route during expected payload transport after the walking Dagger has entered.
Allow sufficient time for a unit payload to traverse all three connected conveyors and emerge at the clear output.
Continue observing well beyond the normal conveyor traversal interval to distinguish a delayed output from a stuck or lost unit.
Zoom in on the route and its output to inspect whether the missing walking unit is visibly represented as a payload or has emerged.
Exit RTS command mode before exercising the reported alternate direct-control path with an untouched Dagger.
Take direct manual control of the upper untouched Dagger using Ctrl-click.
Move the directly controlled Dagger downward toward the conveyor's centerline while keeping it visually identifiable.
Finish aligning the directly controlled Dagger with the payload conveyor centerline.
Place the directly controlled Dagger approximately on the conveyor centerline before moving across it.
Manually drive the possessed Dagger rightward onto the leftmost payload conveyor.
Move the directly controlled Dagger into the first conveyor's footprint so the manual payload-entry control becomes available.
While the possessed Dagger is standing on its current payload conveyor, Ctrl-click that conveyor away from the unit sprite to invoke the manual payload-entry control.
Observe whether the directly controlled Dagger remains visible beyond the conveyor output after the manual-control action.
Move the directly controlled Dagger back onto the rightmost payload conveyor for a more precisely targeted manual-entry attempt.

data.statement: The supplied gameplay save contains an identifiable Dagger and a connected payload-conveyor route; a Dagger entering it should be temporarily represented as a payload and emerge beyond the output rather than be lost.
data.prediction: After selecting and directing one Dagger to the route intake, its walking sprite will vanish at intake, then it will appear as a unit to the right of the third conveyor.
data.observation: In the loaded Sandbox fixture, the outlined middle Dagger was assigned Enter Payload Block and targeted to the leftmost conveyor. It vanished from the walking-unit view and Command Mode reported no selected units. The two untouched Daggers remained visible, while no unit payload or output Dagger was visible after the subsequent 1.2 s, 1 s, 2 s, and 8 s observations.
